newsitem.title: FINLAND: DOUBTS ABOUT NEW OWNER KNOCK AMER.
newsitem.headline: DOUBTS ABOUT NEW OWNER KNOCK AMER.

text.p: Shares in Finnish sporting group Amer fell sharply in lively trade on Tuesday as investors started to doubt the intentions of its new owner Jonathan Bryan Guinness, third Lord Moyne, brokers said.

At 1300/10 GMT, Amer traded at 99.00 markka, down 8.00 or or over seven percent, and two markka below its 101 close on Friday, before news of Moyne's plan to buy control. It surged to 116.50 in late Monday trade after the news.
"The worst fear among investors is that the Lord comes, then chops up the company and disappears," one broker said, speculating that the new owner may plan to strip its assets.
Moyne on Monday said he planned to help Amer boost its key brands, and the purchase was not an "in-and-out situation".
One broker saw new support for the stock at 95 markka.
